interpretations: Per-player average of `double` across their batting_postseason rows (AVG ignores NULLs), joined to `player` on player_id (inner join, so players missing from `player` are dropped); the overall average is the mean of those per-player averages (each player weighted equally); index = player average / overall average; gap = player index − mean index of players sharing the same batting hand; top 10 by gap descending, NULLs last

Same as 1, but the overall average is the mean of all individual postseason `double` values across all records (each record weighted equally, so players with more postseason rows count more), rather than the mean of per-player averages
Same as 1, but the "average index for their batting hand" is computed over individual postseason records for players with that batting hand (record-weighted), rather than over per-player indices
Same as 1, but players with NULL `bats` are treated as their own group (the group's average index is computed among NULL-hand players), so their gap is computed relative to other NULL-hand players
Same as 1, but players with NULL `bats` get a NULL gap (no hand group), and they sort last
Same as 1, but a left join from batting_postseason to `player` keeps players lacking a `player` row (with NULL hand), who then form a NULL-hand group or get a NULL gap

Same as 1, but the per-player average is taken only over records where `double` is non-NULL, and players whose doubles are all NULL (NULL average) are excluded entirely from the overall average and hand averages. Their rows may or may not appear in the output, sorted last as NULL gaps
Same as 1, but players with all-NULL doubles are kept in the output with NULL average, index and gap, and appear at the end of the ordering (only visible if fewer than 10 players have non-NULL gaps)
Same as 1, but "per record" means per player-year-round row in batting_postseason (the default), versus per player-year (summing rounds within a year first, then averaging across years)

Same as 1, but "per record" means per player-team-year-round row, where a player's multiple team entries in the same postseason are treated as separate records (identical to the default, but different if collapsed by team)

Same as 1, but the batting hand is taken as a single value per player from `player.bats`, with values 'L', 'R', 'B' as the groups. Alternatively, 'B' (switch hitters) could be merged into another group, or the groups could be restricted to L and R only
Same as 1, but ties in gap at the 10th place are broken arbitrarily (a plain LIMIT 10), versus including all tied players or breaking ties by player_id

Same as 1, but the output columns are player_id, bats, average doubles, index, and gap with no rounding (full floating-point precision); a variant would show the gap as an absolute difference rather than signed
Same as 1, but "how far each player's index sits above the average index for their batting hand" is interpreted as a ratio (index / hand-average index) rather than a difference
Same as 1, but the hand-average index is computed including the player's own index (a plain group AVG over all players in the hand), versus excluding the player (leave-one-out average)
Some interpretations are missing:

Same as 1, but the overall average of per-player averages is computed over all players in batting_postseason, including those with no matching `player` row, while only matched players appear in the output
Same as 1, but the gap is floored at zero (only "above" the hand average counts, so players below it get 0 or NULL instead of a negative gap)
Same as 1, but empty-string `bats` values are treated as their own group, separate from NULL
Same as 1, but duplicate `player` rows for the same `player_id` fan out the join, which changes the per-player averages and the output rows unless de-duplicated first
Same as 1, but the per-player average is computed over distinct `double` values rather than all records
Same as 1, but the "average index for their batting hand" is the hand's average doubles divided by the overall average, computed from record-level data, rather than the mean of per-player indices
queries:
WITH pa AS (
    SELECT p.player_id, p.bats, AVG(b."double") AS avg_d
    FROM batting_postseason b
    JOIN player p ON b.player_id = p.player_id
    GROUP BY p.player_id, p.bats
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_d) AS o FROM pa
),
idx AS (
    SELECT pa.player_id, pa.bats, pa.avg_d / overall.o AS idx
    FROM pa, overall
)
SELECT player_id,
       idx - AVG(idx) OVER (PARTITION BY bats) AS gap
FROM idx
ORDER BY gap IS NULL, gap DESC
LIMIT 10;
SELECT player_id
FROM batting_postseason
GROUP BY player_id
HAVING AVG(double) > (SELECT AVG(double) FROM batting_postseason);
SELECT bats, AVG(gap) AS avg_gap
FROM (
  SELECT p.bats AS bats, bp.player_id, MAX(bp.year) - MIN(bp.year) AS gap
  FROM batting_postseason bp
  LEFT JOIN player p ON bp.player_id = p.player_id
  GROUP BY bp.player_id
)
GROUP BY bats;
